title: Ephemeral KV resonance and GPU OOMs: runtime protector & fragment compaction
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Multiple customers (hosted, Dedicated, and Private) reported sudden GPU OOM cascades paired with long-tail increases in memory fragmentation. Investigation shows a recurring pattern where ephemeral KV cache entries became internally inconsistent after partial write failures, which caused the allocator to create numerous small slab allocations ('hairline fragments') and prevented timely compaction. When traffic spiked (prefix-heavy chat workloads), the combined effect triggered GPU memory exhaustion and node instability.

Impact: Customer-facing timeouts and service degradation across several clusters. One Dedicated customer degraded to <50% capacity and requested immediate mitigation. Private deployment customer ran into a repeatable repro and escalated to on-call.

Root cause hypothesis: A race during KV write path + tombstone marking caused ephemeral index entries to become unreachable but still reference small GPU allocations. The allocator's LRU/eviction heuristics did not reclaim these quickly because entries were not considered live nor properly tombstoned for background compaction. The result: high fragmentation, OOM under load, and long tail recoveries.

Goal: Ship minimal, safe runtime protector to prevent immediate customer impact and follow with a background compaction and KV reconciliation path to repair inconsistent indexes without live-request disruption. Provide a canary rollout and monitoring so we can safely patch hosted and Dedicated pools and offer a Private upgrade artifact customers can apply.
mitigation_short_term: 1) Deploy emergency limit on per-session KV growth (soft quota) and reject new ephemeral entries when quota hit, returning 429 with retry-after. 2) Enable conservative evictor mode in affected pools to prefer large-block reclamation. 3) Provide customer-facing advisory and temporary configuration to pin model variant with lower prefix KV usage.
proposed_fix_summary: Two-part runtime patch: A) 'Protector' guard that detects stale/unreachable KV index nodes and moves them into a short-lived tombstone journal for deterministic async compaction; B) background compactor that coalesces hairline fragments into reclaimable slabs and updates allocator free lists atomically. The patch includes a small checksum on KV index entries to improve detection and a safe on-disk (journaling) roll-forward to avoid losing entries during crash recovery.
testing_plan: Unit tests for KV index checksum mismatch and tombstone flow; integration in local multi-tenant sim using synthetic chat traces with prefix skew; stress test in staging that ramps to 4x typical load for 72h while validating no OOMs and steady fragment metrics; canary rollout to 3 low-traffic clusters for 48h, then medium clusters for 72h before broader deployment.
acceptance_criteria: No unexpected GPU OOM crashes in canary clusters for 48 hours under synthetic prefix-heavy load
Fragmentation ratio (heap free variance) reduced by >= 40% in canary vs baseline
KV index repair runs complete within configured window and does not increase tail latency > 5%
Affected Dedicated customer confirms restored capacity and no repeat OOMs for 72h after patch
Patch has documented rollback steps and automated feature flag gating
rollback_plan:
Flip feature-flag to conservative evictor mode (already present) and disable protector journaling. If disabling causes reappearance of OOMs, immediately drain affected nodes and revert to previous runtime image. Preserve a copy of the journal for offline forensic reconstruction. Notify ops-runbook channel and on-call leader before revert.

Rollback checklist: 1) Disable protector flag; 2) Drain canary nodes; 3) Redeploy prior image; 4) Monitor OOMs for 6 hours; 5) Inform customers and attach incident notes.
deployment_plan: 1) Build patch branch and open PR (see attachments). 2) Run full CI + stress suite. 3) Canary to 3 low-traffic clusters (hosted) with feature-flag enabled (percentage gate 5%). 4) If stable for 48h, increase to 20% and add two Dedicated pools. 5) Post-check, publish private upgrade package and runbooks for Private customers. 6) Full fleet rollout with staged percentage increases and automated canary checks controlling progression.

long_term_work: Refactor allocator free-list to reduce hairline fragmentation and coalesce small allocations proactively
Add KV index versioning with a compact-on-upgrade path to avoid long live-repair operations
Improve scheduling heuristics to avoid placing high-prefix workloads on low-memory-density nodes
Telemetry: add per-tenant fragmentation heatmap and automatic mitigation recommendations in Console
postmortem_notes: Preliminary: contributing factors include insufficient detection of partially-written KV index nodes, allocator design optimized for throughput over long-term compaction, and lack of early alarms on fragment growth. Action items: complete protector and compactor, harden write-path with checksums, and add SLO-linked alerts for fragmentation metrics.
